claims.text: The proposed intervention is to preheat the LPBF build substrate to approximately 500°C.
Substrate preheating reduces the cooling rate during LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi.
Substrate preheating reduces thermal gradients during solidification.
Reduced cooling rates and thermal gradients produce a more homogeneous elemental distribution.
Substrate preheating reduces compositional segregation in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Thermal moderation from substrate preheating relaxes or lowers residual stresses.
Substrate preheating decreases defect density, including porosity.
Reduced segregation, residual stress, and defect density enhance the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi components.
Preheated LPBF AlCrFeNiSi will have higher yield strength than material made using a room-temperature substrate.
Preheated LPBF AlCrFeNiSi will have greater ductility than material made using a room-temperature substrate.
Preheated LPBF AlCrFeNiSi will perform better overall than conventionally fabricated material.
Room-temperature-substrate LPBF produces greater segregation than preheated-substrate LPBF.
Room-temperature-substrate LPBF produces higher residual stresses than preheated-substrate LPBF.
Room-temperature-substrate LPBF produces more processing-induced defects than preheated-substrate LPBF.
Bulk-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi exhibits more pronounced segregation than the proposed preheated LPBF material.
The proposed effect is bounded to AlCrFeNiSi LPBF conducted in argon, with preheating up to approximately 500°C and otherwise typical laser parameters.
